label: Input textures
summary: A function on an output entry (an internal object of the game's interface engine) that, going by its name, gives the textures that feed into it.
details: The game documents no return type and vanilla never uses it, so what an output entry is and what these textures are stays unclear. The game documents nothing more.

label: Output entry path
summary: A function on an output entry (an internal object of the game's interface engine) that, going by its name, gives its path.
details: The game documents no return type and vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is output entry selected
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the output entry is currently selected.
details: An output entry is an internal object of the game's interface engine. Vanilla never names this function; other types have an IsSelected used to show a button as pressed (for example SaveGameItem.IsSelected in the load game screen), which is only a hint.

label: Is output entry valid
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the output entry exists and can be used.
details: Vanilla never names this function. Elsewhere IsValid follows other things, for example a character's government in a text check, to test that the thing is there; that is only a hint.

label: Output entry itself
summary: A function on an output entry that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the output entry itself. In game texts a function called Self follows other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Toggle output entry selection
summary: An action that, going by its name, switches the output entry between selected and not selected.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Access paged list itself
summary: A function on paged list data (the page state of a list shown a few items at a time) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the paged list data itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, which passes a widget along as a data context, is a different type and only a hint.

label: Can show next page
summary: Yes or no: whether a paged list has a page after the current one.
details: It takes the total number of items in the list. Vanilla uses it as the enabled check of the next page button of the tournament contest choice and of the emblem list in the coat of arms designer, passing the size of that list; going by its name, the button is then off on the last page.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: How many items the whole list has.
fields.values: a whole number, in vanilla GetDataModelSize( list )

label: Can show previous page
summary: Yes or no: whether a paged list has a page before the current one.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled check of the previous page button of the tournament contest choice and of the emblem list in the coat of arms designer; going by its name, the button is then off on the first page.

label: Items on current page
summary: The part of a list that falls on the current page.
details: It takes the full list and hands back only the items of the page being shown. Vanilla uses it as the list source of the tournament contest choice and of the emblem list in the coat of arms designer. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The full list to split into pages.
fields.values: a list (data model), for example ActivityType.GetPickablePhases

label: Current page number
summary: The number of the page a paged list is showing, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as the first half of a page counter like 2 / 5, next to GetMaxPage, in the tournament contest choice and the coat of arms designer.

label: Number of pages
summary: The number of the last page of a paged list, as a whole number.
details: It takes the total number of items in the list. Vanilla shows it as the second half of a page counter like 2 / 5, after GetCurrentPage, in the tournament contest choice and the coat of arms designer.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: How many items the whole list has.
fields.values: a whole number, in vanilla GetDataModelSize( list )

label: Reset paging
summary: An action that, going by its name, resets a paged list to its starting page.
details: It takes the total number of items. Vanilla calls it when the tournament contest choice opens, through ActivityPlanner.AccessPhasePageData, which the same file uses as the data context for the PagedContainerData buttons, so that line very likely belongs to this type. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: How many items the whole list has.
fields.values: a whole number, in vanilla GetDataModelSize( list )

label: Paged list itself
summary: A function on paged list data that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the paged list data itself. Vanilla never names it on this type; lines with Self on other types are only a hint.

label: Items per page
summary: An action that, going by its name, sets how many items a paged list shows on one page.
details: Vanilla sets it to 4 when the tournament contest choice opens, through ActivityPlanner.AccessPhasePageData, which the same file uses as the data context for the PagedContainerData buttons. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: How many items one page shows.

label: Next page
summary: An action that moves a paged list on to its next page.
details: It takes the total number of items in the list. Vanilla calls it from the next page button of the tournament contest choice and of the emblem list in the coat of arms designer. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: How many items the whole list has.
fields.values: a whole number, in vanilla GetDataModelSize( list )

label: Previous page
summary: An action that moves a paged list back to its previous page.
details: Vanilla calls it from the previous page button of the tournament contest choice and of the emblem list in the coat of arms designer. It returns nothing.

label: Access selection tool itself
summary: A function on a parametric select (an internal selection object of the game's interface engine) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Height delta filter on
summary: Whether the map editor's parametric selection uses its height delta filter (yes or no).
details: The parametric selection selects parts of the heightmap by rules. Its Height delta checkbox shows this value, and the minimum and maximum delta boxes can only be edited while it is true. The Select button works when this or the height range filter is on. Going by the name, height delta means the height difference between neighbouring points; the game does not say more.

label: Height range filter on
summary: Whether the map editor's parametric selection uses its height range filter (yes or no).
details: Its Height range checkbox shows this value, and the minimum and maximum height boxes (starting at 0 and 255) can only be edited while it is true. The Select button works when this or the height delta filter is on.

label: Run parametric selection
summary: Carries out the map editor's parametric selection with the filters that are switched on; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the tool's Select button, which is enabled only when the height range or the height delta filter is on. Going by the tool, it selects the parts of the heightmap that match those filters.

label: Selection tool itself
summary: A function on a parametric select that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the object itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Set maximum height delta
summary: Sets the upper limit of the parametric selection's height delta filter from the text box it is attached to; it returns nothing.
details: The map editor calls it whenever the text of the maximum height delta box changes; the box starts at -1 and can be edited only while the height delta filter is on. It takes no argument, so the value comes from the box.

label: Set minimum height delta
summary: Sets the lower limit of the parametric selection's height delta filter from the text box it is attached to; it returns nothing.
details: The map editor calls it whenever the text of the minimum height delta box changes; the box starts at -1 and can be edited only while the height delta filter is on. It takes no argument, so the value comes from the box.

label: Set maximum height
summary: Sets the highest height of the parametric selection's height range filter from the text box it is attached to; it returns nothing.
details: The map editor calls it whenever the text of the maximum height box changes; the box starts at 255 and can be edited only while the height range filter is on. It takes no argument, so the value comes from the box.

label: Set minimum height
summary: Sets the lowest height of the parametric selection's height range filter from the text box it is attached to; it returns nothing.
details: The map editor calls it whenever the text of the minimum height box changes; the box starts at 0 and can be edited only while the height range filter is on. It takes no argument, so the value comes from the box.

label: Toggle parametric selection
summary: Opens or closes the map editor's parametric selection tool, going by its name; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the heightmap tool's "Par" button, whose tooltip reads Parametric selection.

label: Access participant itself
summary: A function on participant info (one participant's entry, seen in a debug window) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the participant info itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Participant character
summary: The character a participant entry is about.
details: Vanilla uses it only in the debug watch window, where it shows the participant's name with GetUINameNotMe. What the participant takes part in is not said there. The game documents no return type.

label: Participant contribution
summary: How much a participant has contributed, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it only in the debug watch window as Contribution: followed by the number. Contribution to what is not documented.

label: Participant itself
summary: A function on participant info that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the participant info itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Access particle data itself
summary: A function on particle user data (an internal object of the game's particle effects) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Particle data ID
summary: Going by its name, the identifier of a particle user data entry, as text.
details: Particle user data is an internal object of the game's particle effects. Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Is particle data selected
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the particle user data entry is selected.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type and the game documents nothing more.

label: Particle data label
summary: Going by its name, the label of a particle user data entry, as text.
details: Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Remove particle data
summary: An action that, going by its name, removes the particle user data entry.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it on this type and the game documents nothing more.

label: Particle data itself
summary: A function on particle user data that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the object itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Toggle particle data selection
summary: An action that, going by its name, switches the particle user data entry between selected and not selected.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Particle data type name
summary: Going by its name, the name of the particle user data's type.
details: The game documents no return type and vanilla never uses it.

label: Particle data type size
summary: Going by its name, the size of the particle user data's type, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more, not even the unit.

label: Access search match itself
summary: A function on a pattern item (one match of the text search in the character list's filter) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the pattern item itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Matched culture
summary: The culture a text search match stands for, when the match is a culture.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter's list of matching items, where it shows the culture's name; the row is shown only when IsCulture is true. The game documents no return type.

label: Matched dynasty
summary: The dynasty a text search match stands for, when the match is a dynasty.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter's list of matching items, where it shows the dynasty's name; the row is shown only when IsDynasty is true. The game documents no return type.

label: Matched faith
summary: The faith a text search match stands for, when the match is a faith.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter's list of matching items, where it shows the faith's icon; the row is shown only when IsFaith is true. A text in the faith view also shows its name. The game documents no return type.

label: Matched government
summary: The government type a text search match stands for, when the match is a government.
details: Vanilla shows its name in the character filter's list of matching items, in a row shown only when IsGovernment is true, and in the character list's government tooltip. The game documents no return type.

label: Matched heritage
summary: The heritage (the group a culture belongs to) a text search match stands for, when the match is a heritage.
details: Vanilla shows its name in the character filter's list of matching items, in a row shown only when IsHeritage is true, and in a character list tooltip. The game documents no return type.

label: Matched house
summary: The dynasty house a text search match stands for, when the match is a house.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter's list of matching items, where it shows the house's name; the row is shown only when IsHouse is true. The game documents no return type.

label: Matched name
summary: The given name a text search match stands for, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter's list of matching items, in the line Given name matches followed by the name in quotes.

label: Matched religion
summary: The religion a text search match stands for, when the match is a religion.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter's list of matching items, where it shows the religion's name; the row is shown only when IsReligion is true. The game documents no return type.

label: Matched rite
summary: The rite a text search match stands for, when the match is a rite.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter's list of matching items, where it shows the rite's icon; the row is shown only when IsRite is true. What a rite is in this filter is not documented. The game documents no return type.

label: Matched trait
summary: The trait a text search match stands for, when the match is a trait.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter's list of matching items, where it shows the trait's name; the row is shown only when IsTrait is true. The game documents no return type.

label: Match kind
summary: Going by its name, the kind of thing a text search match is, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it at the end of every row of the character filter's list of matching items, after the name, trait, faith, house and so on, so it reads as a label of what was matched.

label: Is culture match
summary: Yes or no: whether a text search match is a culture.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter to show the culture row only for culture matches.

label: Is dynasty match
summary: Yes or no: whether a text search match is a dynasty.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter to show the dynasty row only for dynasty matches.

label: Is faith match
summary: Yes or no: whether a text search match is a faith.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter to show the faith row only for faith matches.

label: Is government match
summary: Yes or no: whether a text search match is a government type.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter to show the government row only for government matches.

label: Is heritage match
summary: Yes or no: whether a text search match is a heritage.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter to show the heritage row only for heritage matches.

label: Is house match
summary: Yes or no: whether a text search match is a dynasty house.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter to show the house row only for house matches.

label: Is name match
summary: Yes or no: whether a text search match is a given name.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter to show the Given name matches row only for name matches.

label: Is religion match
summary: Yes or no: whether a text search match is a religion.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter to show the religion row only for religion matches.

label: Is rite match
summary: Yes or no: whether a text search match is a rite.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter to show the rite row only for rite matches.

label: Is match selected
summary: Yes or no: going by its use, whether a text search match is selected in the character filter.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a cross icon on a match row. Which match counts as selected is not documented.

label: Is trait match
summary: Yes or no: whether a text search match is a trait.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character filter to show the trait row only for trait matches.

label: Click search match
summary: The action run when a text search match row in the character filter is clicked.
details: Vanilla calls it from each match row's click, followed by CharacterSelectionList.ClearPattern and ApplyFiltersSort. Exactly what it changes is not documented. It returns nothing.

label: Search match itself
summary: A function on a pattern item that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the text search match itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Access pause menu itself
summary: A function on the pause menu (the in-game menu with save, load and exit) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the pause menu itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Can close lobby
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the multiplayer lobby can be closed from the pause menu.
details: Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Can load game
summary: Yes or no: whether a saved game can be loaded from the pause menu right now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the pause menu's load button, together with a check that no submenu is open. Which conditions block loading is not documented.

label: Close lobby
summary: An action that, going by its name, closes the multiplayer lobby.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Exit game
summary: An action that leaves the running game from the pause menu.
details: It takes a yes or no value; vanilla's exit button passes yes, and what no would change is not documented. The button's text comes from GetExitName. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A yes or no switch; its meaning is not documented.

label: Close lobby tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text for closing the multiplayer lobby.
details: Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Exit button text
summary: The text shown on the pause menu's exit button.
details: Vanilla uses it as the label of the exit button that calls ExitGame. Which wordings it can give is not documented.

label: Has saved games
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether any saved games exist.
details: Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Is lobby open
summary: Yes or no: whether the game is already open as a multiplayer lobby.
details: Vanilla uses it in the pause menu to hide the open lobby and switch character buttons while a lobby is open, together with checks for Ironman and multiplayer.

label: Load game
summary: An action that, going by its name and its use on the pause menu's load button, loads a saved game.
details: Vanilla calls it from the pause menu's load button, which is enabled by CanLoadIngame and has LoadIngameTooltip as its tooltip. It returns nothing.

label: Load game tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the pause menu's load button.
details: Vanilla uses it on the load button; going by the button's enabled check, it probably explains why loading is not possible, but the game does not say.

label: Open lobby
summary: An action that opens the multiplayer lobby from the pause menu.
details: Vanilla calls it from the go to lobby and open lobby buttons; the open lobby button is hidden in Ironman, in multiplayer and while a lobby is already open. It returns nothing.

label: Open settings
summary: An action that opens the game settings from the pause menu.
details: Vanilla calls it from a pause menu button. It returns nothing.

label: Resume game
summary: An action that, going by its name, closes the pause menu and goes back to the game.
details: Vanilla calls it from the pause menu's resume button. It returns nothing.

label: Save game
summary: An action that saves the game from the pause menu.
details: Vanilla calls it from the pause menu's save button. Whether it saves at once or opens the save screen first is not documented. It returns nothing.

label: Pause menu itself
summary: A function on the pause menu that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the pause menu itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Switch character
summary: An action that lets the player switch to playing another character, from the pause menu.
details: Vanilla calls it from the switch character button, which is hidden in Ironman, while a lobby is open and when the game has several players. It returns nothing.

label: Access account itself
summary: A function on the Paradox account object (the player's online account in the game) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the account object itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Account inventory
summary: The inventory of the player's Paradox account.
details: The engine's account screens use it in a test widget the engine keeps for its SDK test code: they check whether the inventory has been retrieved yet and whether it holds a certain item. It is not used in the game's own interface.

label: Last link error
summary: Going by its name, the last error from linking the Paradox account.
details: The game documents no return type and vanilla never uses it.

label: Last link error text
summary: Going by its name, the last account linking error as readable text in the player's language.
details: Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Login provider text key
summary: Going by its name, the localization key for the outside service the account is linked through, as text.
details: Which services count as such providers is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Login provider name
summary: Going by its name, the readable name of the outside service the account is linked through.
details: Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Can link account
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the Paradox account can be linked right now.
details: Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Is logged in
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the player is logged in to their Paradox account.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the login window uses LoginView.IsLoggedIn, a different type, which is only a hint.

label: Account itself
summary: A function on the Paradox account object that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the account object itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Access setting itself
summary: A function on a core setting (one entry of the game's settings) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the setting itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Needs apply
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether a change to the setting only takes effect after it is applied.
details: Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Needs restart
summary: Whether a change to this game setting only takes effect after restarting the game (yes or no).
details: The settings window reaches it through a setting's promoted entry and shows a restart-required mark next to the setting when it is true. The engine's version shows that mark only while the setting has been changed and the window applies changes on restart.

label: Setting itself
summary: A function on a core setting that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the setting itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Access fold-out itself
summary: A function on a fold-out (a section of the interface that can be folded shut and opened) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the fold-out itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Fold section
summary: An action that folds a fold-out section shut.
details: Vanilla calls it from buttons and at the end of an animation in the event windows. It returns nothing.

label: Is folded
summary: Yes or no: whether a fold-out section is folded shut.
details: Vanilla uses it in the event windows to show a button only while the fold-out is folded and the event has fewer than 10 options.

label: Is unfolded
summary: Yes or no: whether a fold-out section is open.
details: Vanilla uses it in many windows, such as the war declaration, activity list and court positions windows, to show a section's content only while it is open.

label: Fold-out itself
summary: A function on a fold-out that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the fold-out itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Set fold state
summary: An action that, going by its name, sets whether a fold-out section is folded or open.
details: It takes one value, which the game does not describe. Vanilla never uses it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The state to set; not documented.

label: Starting fold state
summary: An action that sets whether a fold-out section starts folded or open when it is shown.
details: Vanilla calls it when a window is created, with 'unfolded' in the war declaration and faith windows and with 'folded' in the event windows. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: How the section starts.

label: Toggle section
summary: An action that opens a fold-out section when it is folded, and folds it when it is open.
details: Vanilla calls it from buttons in many windows, for example the silk road window and the shared interface parts. It returns nothing.

label: Unfold section
summary: An action that opens a fold-out section.
details: Vanilla calls it when a window is created, for example in the activity list, culture and decisions windows, so the section starts open. It returns nothing.

label: Access video control itself
summary: A function on a video control (the playback control of a video in the interface) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the video control itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Is video looping
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the video starts over when it ends.
details: Vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more.

label: Is video finished
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the video has played to the end.
details: Vanilla never names Type.Function for it, but the Christian church window reaches a widget's GfxVideoControl and checks IsPlaybackComplete to wait for a page turn video; that is a hint, not proof it is this type.

label: Is video playing
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the video is playing right now.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type; the music player's IsPlaying belongs to another type and is only a hint.

label: Restart video
summary: An action that, going by its name, plays the video again from the start.
details: Vanilla's activity windows reach the event video's GfxVideoControl and call Restart when they start; that is a hint that it is this function. It returns nothing.

label: Video control itself
summary: A function on a video control that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the video control itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Set video looping
summary: An action that, going by its name, sets whether the video starts over when it ends.
details: It takes one value, very likely yes or no, which the game does not describe. Vanilla never uses it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether to loop; not documented.

label: Start video
summary: An action that, going by its name, starts playing the video.
details: It returns nothing. The vanilla lines with this name are game texts using the word Start, not uses of this function.

label: Stop video
summary: An action that, going by its name, stops the video.
details: It returns nothing. The vanilla lines with this name are game texts using the word Stop, not uses of this function.

label: Access tab itself
summary: A function on a tab item (one tab of a tab bar in the interface) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the tab item itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type; vanilla passes PdxGuiTabItem.Self instead.

label: Tab key
summary: The key that names a tab, as text.
details: Vanilla compares it with a fixed key to treat one tab differently, for example the saints tab of the faith window, and the shared tab bar shows it in a debug text. Going by those uses, it is the key the tab was added with in PdxGuiTabs.AddTab.

label: Tab title
summary: The display text of a tab, looked up from its key.
details: It takes a text that vanilla sets per window, such as 'lobby_tab' or 'situation_tab'; going by those uses it is a prefix that is combined with the tab's key to find the localized title, but the game does not say so.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A prefix for the tab's text key, going by vanilla's use.

label: Tab itself
summary: The tab item itself, to pass on to another function.
details: Vanilla's shared tab bar passes it to PdxGuiTabs.SetTab when a tab is clicked and to PdxGuiTabs.IsTabItemSet to show the chosen tab as pressed. The game documents no return type.

label: Access table row itself
summary: A function on a table row of the interface that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the row itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Row number
summary: Going by its name, the position of the row in its table, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type, and the lines with this name belong to other types. Whether counting starts at 0 or 1 is not documented.

label: Table row itself
summary: A function on a table row that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the row itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Access tab bar itself
summary: A function on a tab bar (a set of tabs in an interface window) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the tab bar itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Add tab
summary: An action that adds a tab with the given key to the tab bar.
details: Vanilla calls it when a window is created, for example 'character' in the multiplayer lobby and 'rites' and 'tenets' in the faith window. The key is what GetKey, IsTabSet and SetTabByKey refer to. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The new tab's key.

label: Add tab if
summary: An action that adds a tab with the given key only when a condition is true.
details: Vanilla's multiplayer lobby adds the landless rulers tab only when that DLC feature is present. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The new tab's key.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The condition; the tab is added only when it is true.
fields.values: a yes or no value, for example HasDlcFeature( 'landless_playable' )

label: Active tab
summary: Going by its name, the tab that is currently chosen in the tab bar.
details: The game documents no return type and vanilla never uses it.

label: Tabs
summary: The list of tabs in the tab bar.
details: Vanilla's shared tab bar uses it as the list of tab buttons to draw, and hides the bar when it has only one tab.

label: Is tab chosen
summary: Yes or no: whether the given tab item is the chosen tab.
details: Vanilla's shared tab bar uses it with PdxGuiTabItem.Self to show the chosen tab's button as pressed.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tab item to check.
fields.values: a tab item, in vanilla PdxGuiTabItem.Self

label: Is tab open
summary: Yes or no: whether the tab with the given key is the chosen tab.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a tab's content only while that tab is chosen, for example the character and landless rulers tabs of the multiplayer lobby.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the tab to check.

label: Listen for tab change
summary: An action that, going by its name and use, makes the tab bar react to a named signal.
details: Vanilla's multiplayer lobby calls it on creation with 'lobby_window_change_tab'; no other file names that text, so what sends the signal and what it does is not shown. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the signal to listen for.

label: Remove tab
summary: An action that, going by its name, removes a tab from the tab bar.
details: It takes one value, probably the tab's key as with AddTab, but the game does not say. Vanilla never uses it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tab to remove; not documented.

label: Remove tab if
summary: An action that, going by its name, removes a tab from the tab bar when a condition is true.
details: It takes two values, probably the tab's key and a condition as with AddTabIf, but the game does not say. Vanilla never uses it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tab to remove; not documented.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The condition; not documented.

label: Tab bar itself
summary: A function on a tab bar that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the tab bar itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Reset tab when shown
summary: An action that, going by its name, sets whether the tab bar resets its chosen tab each time the window is shown.
details: Vanilla passes yes in the multiplayer lobby and no in the faith window. Going by the name, the faith window then keeps its last chosen tab; which tab a reset goes to is not documented. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether to reset.

label: Choose tab
summary: An action that makes the given tab item the chosen tab.
details: Vanilla's shared tab bar calls it with PdxGuiTabItem.Self when a tab button is clicked. To choose a tab by its key, SetTabByKey is used instead. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The tab item to choose.
fields.values: a tab item, in vanilla PdxGuiTabItem.Self

label: Choose tab by key
summary: An action that makes the tab with the given key the chosen tab.
details: Vanilla uses it to open a window on a set tab, for example 'tenets' in the faith window, or picks the key with SelectLocalization in the administrative vassal window. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the tab to choose.

label: Access tree table itself
summary: A function on a tree table (a table whose rows can be expanded to show child rows) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the tree table itself. The game documents no return type and vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Can expand row
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the given row of a tree table has child rows to expand.
details: It takes one value, probably the row, which the game does not describe. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The row to check; not documented.

label: Expand row
summary: An action that, going by its name, opens a row of a tree table to show its child rows.
details: It takes one value, probably the row, which the game does not describe. Vanilla never uses it; the lines with this name are game texts using the word Expand. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The row to expand; not documented.

label: Row depth
summary: Going by its name, how deep a row sits in the tree table, as a whole number.
details: It takes one value, probably the row, which the game does not describe. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The row; not documented.

label: Row indent
summary: Going by its name, how far a row of the tree table is indented, as a two-number offset.
details: It takes two values that the game does not describe. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Not documented.

label: Number of child rows
summary: Going by its name, how many child rows a row of the tree table has, as a whole number.
details: It takes one value, probably the row, which the game does not describe. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The row; not documented.

label: Is row expanded
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether a row of the tree table is open.
details: It takes one value, probably the row, which the game does not describe. Vanilla never uses it on this type; IsExpanded on messages and notifications belongs to other types.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The row to check; not documented.

label: Tree table itself
summary: A function on a tree table that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the tree table itself. Vanilla never names it on this type.

label: Toggle row
summary: An action that, going by its name, opens a row of the tree table when it is closed and closes it when it is open.
details: It takes one value, probably the row, which the game does not describe. Vanilla never uses it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The row; not documented.

label: Collapse row
summary: An action that, going by its name, closes a row of the tree table so its child rows are hidden.
details: It takes one value, probably the row, which the game does not describe. Vanilla never uses it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The row; not documented.

label: Child widget
summary: The child widget (part of the interface inside the current one) with the given name.
details: Vanilla's task contract window uses it to reach the named parts of a letter and start their show animation. It returns a widget, so further widget functions can follow it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the child widget.

label: Parent widget
summary: The widget that contains the current one.
details: Vanilla follows it with FindChild to look at a sibling part, for example to count the visible entries of a tab in the main interface, or with GetIndexInDataModel. The game documents no return type.

label: Widget itself
summary: The current widget itself, to pass on to another function.
details: Vanilla's activity windows pass it to GetEventWindowInsert as a data context. The game documents no return type.

label: Visible child count
summary: Going by its name, how many of the widget's child parts are visible, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses CountVisibleChildren after AccessParent.FindChild, for example to hide a tab when it has no visible entries or to show a count in the faith view; FindChild's return type is not shown, so that is a strong hint rather than proof.

label: Stop live value updates
summary: Ends live updating of a value while a map editor slider is dragged; it returns nothing.
details: The game marks it for the map editor's internal use. The brush settings sliders call it when a change finishes, as the counterpart to EnableValueUpdate at the start of the change. What exactly stops updating is not documented.

label: Start live value updates
summary: Starts live updating of a value while a map editor slider is dragged; it returns nothing.
details: The game marks it for the map editor's internal use. The brush settings sliders call it when a change starts, and DisableValueUpdate when it finishes; in between, each change is passed on to the brush value. What exactly is updated is not documented.
